failingAssertions.case: rerun reads the real runner > archives smoke 3/0 and is SATISFIED on the runner real bytes
failingAssertions.why: This is FN-u9-rerun-parser-expects-labeled-line reproduced at the boundary. The fake runner emits the real ladder runner's bytes; GROUP_LINE (/^([a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*):\s+(.*)$/) matches nothing in them, runGroup's row is undefined, and the archive records 0/0. The run then prints EXACT_MAIN_LADDER_MISSING and exits 1 - exactly what the U9 main proof recorded on 45d6134289051d316257641284976a2f9789ceed.

failingAssertions.case: rerun reads the real runner > archives 2/1 and stays MISSING when the summary reports a failure
failingAssertions.why: Playwright's two-line failure summary ('  1 failed' then '  2 passed (8.1s)') is unreadable to the U9 parser. The VERDICT is right for the wrong reason - MISSING because nothing was read at all, not because a row failed - so the receipt is a lie about what the run proved. The case asserts the archived numbers separately from the verdict precisely so that distinction is held.

failingAssertions.case: rerun reads the real runner > archives 2/1 and stays MISSING when the summary reports a flake
failingAssertions.why: Same unreadable-summary cause, and it also pins the decision this unit records: a flaky row counts as FAILED, because a row that only went green on retry is not 'ran clean against this exact commit'.

requiredEditRevision2.why: Lane A review (.sisyphus/roadmap-completion-20260912/u9b-lane-a-review-pass1-20260917.md, finding 1, MEDIUM) found that the installed Playwright 1.57.0 list/line reporter emits a summary word the U9b regex does not recognise: `interrupted`. Mixed with a clean `N passed` line and no explicit `failed` line, the unrecognised row is silently dropped and the run reads as coverage - a FALSE SATISFIED, which inverts the module's stated fail-closed posture. This section records the revision-2 red run: the new pin cases were added FIRST, against the U9b module exactly as it stands at PR #1815 head 08a74231173b901144605695208f0c4f356c5d7d, before any product line was touched.

N errors were not a part of any test, see above for details
reporterSourceRead.secondMissedTokenFound: Besides `interrupted`, generateSummaryMessage's last token counts FATAL ERRORS rather than tests: `${fatalErrors.length === 1 ? '1 error was not a part of any test' : fatalErrors.length + ' errors were not a part of any test'}, see above for details`. It is pushed only when `fatalErrors.length && expected + unexpected.length + interrupted.length + flaky.length > 0`, i.e. only when at least one test ran - precisely the shape that rides behind a clean `N passed` line. The U9b regex misses it too, so it produces the same false SATISFIED, and the charter's clause 'if generateSummaryMessage emits any other word the regex still misses, cover it the same way and pin it' applies.
reporterSourceRead.nonSummaryLinesRuledOut: The indented per-test headers pushed after `failed`/`interrupted`/`flaky` come from formatTestHeader with `{ indent: '    ' }` and no `index`, so they start with spaces then `[chromium]` - never a leading digit - and cannot match either regex.

failingAssertions.case: rerun reads the real runner > archives 2/1 and stays MISSING when the summary reports an interruption
failingAssertions.why: The injected runner prints the reporter's own spelling, `  1 interrupted` then `  2 passed (7.4s)`. PLAYWRIGHT_SUMMARY's alternation has no `interrupted`, so `if (!summary) continue;` drops the row entirely: the interrupted test is counted neither as passed nor as failed, the archive records 2/0, and the CLI prints SATISFIED and exits 0 (proved by R4) although a test never completed.

failingAssertions.case: rerun reads the real runner > archives 2/1 and stays MISSING when a fatal error rode beside the passes
failingAssertions.why: Same silent-drop cause on the other missed token: `  2 passed (6.2s)` then `  1 error was not a part of any test, see above for details`. A fatal error raised outside any test is not a test failure Playwright can attribute, but it is still a run that did not complete clean, and the archive currently records it as 2/0 coverage.
